title: Ask the Tool, Don't Guess: Agent Tool Calls Hold Their Progress, and the Serving System Should Read It
abstract: arXiv:2609.18849v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: An agentic request spends substantial wall-clock time waiting for tools, and its KV cache holds GPU memory the whole time. Serving systems decide whether that cache stays, leaves, or comes back by guessing how long the tool will run, from the tool's name, its history, a duration declared before the call, or the engine's own occupancy. We show that no estimate fixed before a call starts can know its duration, and such estimates may not even rank the calls. Meanwhile, the running tool already holds the answer, but the agent stack together with the tool silences it. We propose that tool calls report their progress explicitly while they run, and we measure what that takes. A census of four public agent corpora finds a readable signal in most tool time once it is revealed, in two strengths: a fraction of the work remaining, or an accurate signal that the end is near. translated_title: 询问工具，而非猜测：智能体工具调用持有其进度信息，服务系统应当读取它
translated_abstract: 一个智能体请求会花费大量的实际等待时间用于等待工具执行，期间其KV缓存一直占用着GPU显存。服务系统通过猜测工具的运行时长来决定该缓存是保留、释放还是恢复——猜测依据包括工具名称、历史记录、调用前声明的时长，或引擎自身的占用情况。我们证明了任何在调用开始前固定的估计都无法得知其真实时长，这些估计甚至可能无法对调用进行正确排序。与此同时，正在运行的工具本身已经持有答案，但智能体栈与工具共同将其屏蔽了。我们提出工具调用应在运行过程中显式报告其进度，并测量了实现这一目标所需的成本。对四个公开智能体语料库的普查发现，一旦被揭示，大多数工具时间中都存在可读取的信号，且有两种强度：剩余工作的比例，或表明即将结束的准确信号。一个测试框架可以在不改变智能体所见内容的情况下恢复该信号，且没有可测量的（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 论文提出工具调用应在运行时显式报告进度信号（如剩余工作比例或即将结束的准确信号），使服务系统能基于真实进度智能管理KV缓存，而非依赖调用前无法准确的时长猜测。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes that tool calls should explicitly report their progress while running, enabling serving systems to make informed KV cache management decisions based on actual progress signals rather than unreliable pre-call duration estimates.
